post-rpm-ideal-rindler-phase-reception.physical_scope: Additional adopted local phase-reading idealization for the smooth stationary right-wedge Rindler congruence and an affine monochromatic vacuum plane wave with constant future null covector in flat Minkowski spacetime. Exact instantaneous phase readings within this model; finite apparatus interpretation is limited to short observation intervals and wavelengths small relative to the observer's acceleration length. No empirical validation, numerical error bound, detector response, photon-energy identification, or extension of the published SR postulate is asserted.

post-rpm-ideal-rindler-phase-reception:
## Postulate

In the flat affine Minkowski model with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and $x^0=ct$, use the smooth right-wedge chart and stationary congruence of [[pthm-sr-rindler-horizons-and-radar]]. A stationary observer has fixed $\rho>0,y,z$, worldline $z(\tau)$ on an open proper-time interval in seconds, and four-velocity $U=dz/d\tau$ with $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$. These are accelerated timelike worldlines, not global inertial frames.

Let $\theta$ be the dimensionless affine phase with constant nonzero future null covector $k=d\theta$ and ideal vacuum rays of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (i). As an **additional local reception assumption**, adopt that an ideal point receiver comoving with a stationary Rindler observer assigns, at the event $z(\tau)$, the instantaneous received angular frequency

$$\omega(\tau):=-\frac{d(\theta\circ z)}{d\tau}=-k(U(\tau))>0,$$

and linear frequency $\nu(\tau)=\omega(\tau)/(2\pi)$ in the conventions of [[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]] and [[def-sr-si-units-and-coordinate-conventions]]. The phase derivative and positivity are mathematical facts of [[lem-sr-phase-rate-along-worldline]]; their identification with this ideal receiver's reading is the assumption adopted here. This is the pointwise equivalence to the momentarily comoving inertial phase receiver, together with the proper-time clock convention of [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]. Reception comparisons use one and the same affine wave and events joined by one of its radial rays. This assumption does not postulate an emitter mechanism.

The instantaneous quantity may vary along an accelerated worldline. It is not an assertion that an observer's entire proper-time signal is monochromatic or that an arbitrary finite-duration Fourier measurement equals this value. For possible finite-apparatus use, define the local wavelength $\lambda_{\rm loc}:=2\pi c/\omega$ and the translational acceleration length $L_\alpha:=c^2/\alpha$, where $\alpha$ is the observer's proper-acceleration magnitude; for this congruence $L_\alpha=\rho$. The intended local ray regime has $\lambda_{\rm loc}/L_\alpha\ll1$ throughout the observation segment, receiver size small relative to $L_\alpha$, and an observation duration long enough for several cycles but short relative to $L_\alpha/c$. These qualitative scale separations give no numerical tolerance or measured uncertainty. The equality above is exact only inside the adopted ideal model; no accuracy claim for a real receiver follows from it.

This supplements, without changing, the accelerated-reception exclusion in [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] (iv). It includes no detector dynamics, intensity, polarization, finite-bandwidth pulse or envelope, medium, dispersion, absorption, quantum or gravity model, no energy identification with $\hbar\omega$, and no empirical outcome or proof of the model's applicability. It is a sourced adopted idealization, not a deductive or experimentally established law.

pthm-rpm-rindler-clock-gradient.physical_scope: Exact coordinate and proper-time calculations in the right wedge of flat Minkowski spacetime for the stated uniformly accelerated congruence and idealized radial null rays. The clock ratio is conditional on the adopted ideal-clock postulate. The instantaneous received-frequency ratio is conditional on the additional ideal local phase-reception postulate; its finite-apparatus use carries the short-observation and local ray-regime limits, without a numerical accuracy claim. No measurement, material clock model, global accelerated frame, or claim about real clocks or light is asserted.

pthm-rpm-rindler-clock-gradient:
## Statement

Use the flat affine Minkowski model with signature $(-,+,+,+)$ and SI coordinates $(x^0,x^1,y,z)=(ct,x^1,y,z)$. Fix $a>0$ in metres per second squared and define

$$\Phi_a(T,\rho,y,z)=\bigl(\rho\sinh(aT/c),\rho\cosh(aT/c),y,z\bigr),\qquad T\in\mathbb R,\quad \rho>0.$$

Then $\Phi_a$ is a smooth chart of the right wedge $W=\{x^1>|x^0|\}$, with $\rho$ in metres and $T$ in seconds. Its pullback metric, the proper-time rate of a stationary Rindler observer, and that observer's proper-acceleration magnitude are

$$ds^2=-\frac{a^2\rho^2}{c^2}\,dT^2+d\rho^2+dy^2+dz^2,\qquad \frac{d\tau}{dT}=\frac{a\rho}{c^2},\qquad \alpha=\frac{c^2}{\rho}.$$

For ideal radial vacuum rays with $y,z$ fixed, $d\rho/dT=\pm a\rho/c$. A ray joining positive radii $\rho_E,\rho_R$ therefore has one-way Rindler travel time $\Delta T=(c/a)|\log(\rho_R/\rho_E)|$, and stationary ideal clocks at those radii satisfy $\Delta\tau_R/\Delta\tau_E=\rho_R/\rho_E$ over any common nonzero $T$ interval. The clock statement is conditional on the ideal-clock adoption in [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]].

For a future null plane-wave covector $k$ directed along the same radial ray, define $\omega_n=-k(U_n)$ using [[def-sr-null-wave-covector-and-observer-frequency]]. Under the additional adopted local reception rule [[post-rpm-ideal-rindler-phase-reception]], the instantaneous received angular frequencies at the two events obey $\omega_R/\omega_E=\rho_E/\rho_R$. The ratio is exact within that ideal model and inherits its local ray-regime and finite-apparatus qualifications, with no numerical error bound or empirical validation. Clause (iv) of [[post-sr-ideal-plane-wave-model]] retains its accelerated-reception exclusion; this theorem uses the separately adopted rule. The coordinate chart excludes $\rho=0$; no global rigid accelerated frame is asserted.

pthm-rpm-constant-electric-orbit.physical_scope: Exact global coordinate-time solutions of the adopted flat external-field charged test-particle model for a uniform constant electric field, with fixed SI conventions and a smooth explicit potential. The force law is conditional on the local RPM action postulate and its draft equivalence and mass-shell suppliers. No self-field, radiation reaction, measurement, or empirical claim is included.

pthm-rpm-constant-electric-orbit:
## Statement

In the flat Minkowski specialization of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]], adopt the fixed-endpoint external-charge action [[post-rpm-external-charge-action]], its conditional stationary-action equivalence [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]], the flat massive-particle momentum model [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure required by the current local IVP and action-equivalence carriers. Let $m>0$ in kilograms, $q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs, $c>0$ in metres per second, and $E_0\in\mathbb R$ in newtons per coulomb; let the uniform field in one named inertial SI chart be $\mathbf E=E_0e_1$, $\mathbf B=0$. A smooth global potential is $\phi=-E_0x^1$, $\mathbf A=0$, so the local-potential hypothesis is satisfied. Spatial coordinates are in metres, coordinate time $t$ is in seconds, and initial momenta are in kilograms metres per second. Set $F_0=qE_0$ (newtons), take initial event $(0,\mathbf x_0)$ and initial momentum $\mathbf p_0=(p_{01},\mathbf p_\perp)$ at $t=0$, and define $\Pi$ (momentum units), $\mathcal E$ (joules) and $\mathbf v$ (metres per second) by

$$p_1(t)=p_{01}+F_0t,\qquad \Pi=\sqrt{m^2c^2+|\mathbf p_\perp|^2}>0,\qquad \mathcal E(t)=c\sqrt{\Pi^2+p_1(t)^2},\qquad \mathbf v(t)=\frac{c(p_1(t)e_1+\mathbf p_\perp)}{\sqrt{\Pi^2+p_1(t)^2}}.$$

If $F_0\ne0$, the exact position for every $t\in\mathbb R$ is

$$x^1(t)=x^1_0+\frac c{F_0}\left(\sqrt{\Pi^2+p_1(t)^2}-\sqrt{\Pi^2+p_{01}^2}\right),$$
$$\mathbf x_\perp(t)=\mathbf x_{\perp0}+\frac{c\mathbf p_\perp}{F_0}\log\!\left(\frac{p_1(t)+\sqrt{\Pi^2+p_1(t)^2}}{p_{01}+\sqrt{\Pi^2+p_{01}^2}}\right).$$

If $F_0=0$, the field exerts no force on the particle and the orbit is free:
$\mathbf p(t)=\mathbf p_0$, $\mathcal E(t)=\mathcal E(0)$ and
$\mathbf x(t)=\mathbf x_0+c^2\mathbf p_0t/\mathcal E(0)$. These formulas define future-timelike worldlines for all finite coordinate times; any model solution with the same data agrees with them on every common connected time interval. This is a conditional model deduction, not evidence that the adopted action describes a measured particle.

pthm-rpm-constant-magnetic-helix.physical_scope: Exact global coordinate-time solutions of the adopted flat external-field charged test-particle model for a uniform constant magnetic field. pthm-rpm-constant-magnetic-helix:
## Statement

Use the flat SI charged-particle model and local external-action adoption of [[def-rpm-charge-spin-model]] and [[post-rpm-external-charge-action]], with the conditional equation and coordinate Lorentz force of [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]] and [[pthm-rpm-charge-mass-shell]], adopt the flat massive-particle momentum model [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], and assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ of [[def-countable-choice]] for the canonical tangent-bundle smooth structure required by the current local IVP and action-equivalence carriers. Let $m>0$ be in kilograms, $q\in\mathbb R$ in coulombs, $c>0$ in metres per second, and $B_0\in\mathbb R$ in tesla; $\mathbf E=0$, $\mathbf B=B_0e_3$. The smooth global potential $\phi=0$, $\mathbf A=(-B_0x^2/2,B_0x^1/2,0)$ has $\nabla\times\mathbf A=B_0e_3$. Spatial coordinates are in metres, coordinate time $t$ in seconds, and initial momentum components in kilograms metres per second. Given initial position $\mathbf x_0$ and momentum $\mathbf p_0=(p_{01},p_{02},p_{03})$ at $t=0$, define

$$S_0=\sqrt{m^2c^2+|\mathbf p_0|^2},\qquad \gamma_0=S_0/(mc),\qquad \Omega=\frac{qB_0}{\gamma_0m}.$$

Here $S_0$ has momentum units, $\gamma_0$ is dimensionless, and the signed angular frequency $\Omega$ has units of inverse seconds; all displayed positions are in metres and $\mathcal E$ is in joules.

For $\Omega\ne0$, the exact momentum and energy are

$$p_1(t)=p_{01}\cos(\Omega t)+p_{02}\sin(\Omega t),\quad p_2(t)=p_{02}\cos(\Omega t)-p_{01}\sin(\Omega t),\quad p_3(t)=p_{03},\quad \mathcal E(t)=cS_0,$$

and the exact position is

$$x^1(t)=x^1_0+\frac{c}{S_0\Omega}\bigl(p_{01}\sin(\Omega t)+p_{02}(1-\cos(\Omega t))\bigr),$$
$$x^2(t)=x^2_0+\frac{c}{S_0\Omega}\bigl(p_{02}\sin(\Omega t)-p_{01}(1-\cos(\Omega t))\bigr),\qquad x^3(t)=x^3_0+\frac{cp_{03}}{S_0}t.$$

The transverse projection is a circle of radius $|\mathbf p_\perp|/|qB_0|$ when $\mathbf p_\perp=(p_{01},p_{02})\ne0$; it is a straight line parallel to $e_3$ when $\mathbf p_\perp=0$. If $p_{03}=0$ the circular orbit is planar. The field does no work. If $\Omega=0$ (including $q=0$ or $B_0=0$), the solution is free motion $\mathbf p(t)=\mathbf p_0$, $\mathcal E=cS_0$, $\mathbf x(t)=\mathbf x_0+c\mathbf p_0t/S_0$. These formulas give a global future-timelike orbit and are unique on every common connected time interval; they are conditional model deductions, not empirical claims.

pthm-rpm-crossed-field-drift.physical_scope: Exact conditional flat-space statement for constant perpendicular electric and magnetic fields in the adopted external charged test-particle model. When $|E|<c|B|$, a subluminal passive boost removes the electric field and every solution is the inverse boost of a uniform-magnetic-field orbit. A constant drift-velocity solution is singled out, but the theorem does not claim that all particle velocities equal the drift velocity. Null and supercritical crossed fields are excluded; no self-field, radiation reaction, measurement, or empirical claim is made.

pthm-rpm-crossed-field-drift:
## Statement

In the flat SI charged-particle model with adopted action, conditional force equation, flat massive-particle momentum model, and $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ assumption required by the current local RPM carriers [[post-rpm-external-charge-action]], [[pthm-rpm-external-charge-action-equivalence]], [[pthm-rpm-charge-mass-shell]], [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]], and [[def-countable-choice]], let $m>0$ be in kilograms, $q$ in coulombs, $c$ in metres per second, $E_0$ in newtons per coulomb, and $B_0$ in tesla. Use an inertial chart with $x^0=ct$ and all coordinates in metres, so $t$ is in seconds. Set $\mathbf E=E_0e_1$, $\mathbf B=B_0e_3$, $B_0\ne0$, and $|E_0|<c|B_0|$. Use the smooth combined potential $\phi=-E_0x^1$, $\mathbf A=(-B_0x^2/2,B_0x^1/2,0)$. Define

$$\mathbf v_d=\frac{\mathbf E\times\mathbf B}{|\mathbf B|^2}=-\frac{E_0}{B_0}e_2,\qquad \gamma_d=(1-|\mathbf v_d|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}.$$

The drift velocity has units of metres per second and $\gamma_d$ is dimensionless.

The passive Lorentz boost of velocity $\mathbf v_d$ transforms these fields to $\mathbf E'=0$, $\mathbf B'=\mathbf B/\gamma_d$. Consequently every flat-model solution in the laboratory frame is the inverse boost of the uniform-magnetic-field orbit of [[pthm-rpm-constant-magnetic-helix]] with the boosted initial data. The laboratory coordinate time increases strictly and ranges over all real values along that inverse-boosted orbit. In particular, the constant velocity $\mathbf v=\mathbf v_d$ is an exact solution because $\mathbf E+\mathbf v_d\times\mathbf B=0$. Other initial data give boosted helical orbits; the theorem does not identify every velocity with $\mathbf v_d$. The cases $|E_0|=c|B_0|$ and $|E_0|>c|B_0|$ are outside the statement.
